The Vue compiled render uses `with(this)` — incompatible with strict ESM/esbuild. Solution: compile templates with `{ outputSourceRange:false }` won't help; instead use `compiler.compileToFunctions`? Simplest: keep `with` but mark the onLoad output as non-strict by setting loader options... esbuild rejects `with` in ESM.

Alternative: set the script output as CommonJS (no strict) — esbuild still rejects `with` in any module. Best: obtain render function via `compiler.compileToFunctions(template)` which returns render code as a `new Function` string (uses with internally, returns function). Then assign `__comp.render = new Function(code)(...)`. Actually `compileToFunctions` returns actual functions. But I'm serializing to text.

Simpler approach: wrap the compiled render in `new Function`. `compileToFunctions(template)` returns `{render, staticRenderFns}` actual functions. I can't serialize functions. But I can, in the plugin, generate:
```
__comp.render = new Function(<render code string wrapped>).call(...)
```
The render code is `with(this){return ...}`. `new Function('with(this){return ...}')` works in non-strict. So generate: `__comp.render = new Function(${JSON.stringify(renderCode)});` — but the code references `_c` etc via `this`, so `function(){ with(this){...} }.call(vm)`. Actually `__comp.render` should be a function; `new Function(code)` yields `function anonymous(){ with(this){...} }` — perfect, Vue calls it with vm as `this`.

For staticRenderFns: array of code strings → map to new Function.
